howToPage.poradnikTytul: How to record rap at home — step by step
howToPage.poradnikWstep: No studio or expensive gear needed. A mic, headphones and a browser are enough. Here is the whole path from beat to finished track:

k1.tekst: Open the <bity>free beats</bity> and listen without an account. Filter by genre, tempo (BPM) and key. Look for a beat that fits your flow, not just one that sounds nice.

k2.tytul: Set up your gear and room
k2.tekst: A USB mic, or even a headset mic, is fine to start. Record with headphones so the beat does not bleed into the mic. Pick the quietest room — blankets, curtains or a wardrobe full of clothes kill echo better than a bare wall.

k3.tekst: Create an account and do a short test. Stay about a hand's width from the mic and set the mic level in your system so your loudest lines do not clip. A bit too quiet beats too loud — clipping stays forever.

k4.tekst: Record in the online Studio in your browser or in the <nagrywarka>Windows Recorder</nagrywarka>. Do several takes — that is what “Record again” is for. Take length depends on your plan.

k5.tytul: Build the track in the Studio
k5.tekst: Trim the take, place it on the timeline and add more tracks: doubles, a hook, ad-libs. The number of tracks depends on your plan.

k6.tekst: Ask BITEK for a mix and master proposal. It balances your vocal with the beat and prepares a streaming-ready master. You decide whether to accept the change.

k7.tekst: Download the finished file in your plan's quality or publish it in the <utwory>tracks catalogue</utwory>, where others can listen and rate it. Credit the beat's author before publishing.

recorderPage.metaTitle: Vocal recorder for Windows — free download
recorderPage.metaDescription: Two ways to record on BitRymDym: the Windows app and the browser studio. What the app does, and what stays on the site.
recorderPage.title: Two ways to record
recorderPage.lead: The account, plan and limits are the same. The Windows app records a vocal on the computer. The site arranges the song, the mix and the master. The site terms cover the app, because it uses the same account.
recorderPage.downloadNote: Downloading and signing in to the app both need an account on the site. The installer is for Windows. It does not need an administrator. The shortcut is named BitRymDym. The installer includes ffmpeg and ffplay, so beat monitoring works without extra programs. A Mac and Apple version is coming soon. Until then, on a Mac you record in the browser.
recorderPage.windowsLead: You sign in with the same address as on the site. The app loads published beats and records only the microphone.
can: Sign in to an existing account and sign out. With the 48-hour password box ticked, the password sits hidden in a file encrypted with your Windows account key, for up to 48 hours after your last sign-in. Signing out deletes it and also ends the session on the server.
Open Studio Online: a beat from the site catalog plays as a monitor and is not saved to disk.
With Premium Gold open Studio Offline: your own beat file on the computer, 16 vocal tracks and 6 for doubles and adlibs.
Record the microphone to a plain WAV file, one channel, at the same quality as the site.
Turn on a count-in before recording: 1, 2 or 4 bars of clicks at the beat tempo. The clicks are not part of the recording.
Add vocal tracks up to the plan limit. The beat lane does not count. One track holds many recordings side by side.
See the waveform and time on the timeline, zoom in, and move recordings, also to another track.
Cut, copy, paste, split and delete a selected span. Edits do not change the WAV file, and Undo brings back the previous state.
Mute a track with M and solo it with S. A muted track is not uploaded.
Set volume from −24 dB to +12 dB and pan: −100 left, 0 centre, +100 right. You hear it at once.
Choose the microphone and the listening output separately, such as speakers or Bluetooth headphones. The app remembers the choice.

Line the voice up with the beat by itself: after a recording the app listens for the faint trace of the beat in the microphone, works out the delay and moves the vocal. It remembers it for this gear. When the beat cannot be heard, for example in Bluetooth headphones, press Zmierz (Measure) and clap along with the clicks. You can also type the delay in.
Bring a project back after a crash or a close: when you enter the Studio, the app asks whether to restore it.
Check the microphone with the mic test: a level bar and a hint (too quiet, good, too loud). Nothing is saved.
After Stop, get a rating of the recording (clipping, near silence, quiet, or good level) and a warning when the mic dropped samples or vanished mid-recording.
Check by itself whether a new version exists. When you click Update it downloads, verifies and installs it. Nothing happens during recording or an upload.
Send the recordings to Studio as a project and open it in the browser. The upload runs in the background. If the network drops, the next try finishes the same project, even after restarting the app.
In Gold download stems: every vocal track as its own WAV from the start of the song.
recorderPage.cannotTitle: What the app does not do
cannot: A Mac and Apple version is coming soon. The app does not load other people's VST plugins.
The beat is not mixed into the vocal file. Only the vocal is uploaded.
It does not play two mixes at once, such as beat-only in headphones and mic plus beat on speakers.
While recording, it does not feed your own voice back into the headphones.
When the microphone does not hear the beat at all, the app cannot measure the delay. Then press Zmierz (Measure) next to the delay, or move the recording on the timeline.
It has no effects or tuning. Volume and left or right are heard in the app, but only the dry vocal goes to the account. On the site you set them in Studio, with the cut, volume over time and notes.
It has no samples. You add them in Studio on the site, with the piano and the notes.
It does not make the mix, the master, master approval, lyrics, cover, video or a listen link. BITEK does the mix and the master on the site.
From Silver in Studio on the site: ducking under the beat (the vocal dips when the beat hits) and pitch other than zero (you raise or lower the recording).
Speakers next to an open microphone bleed into the recording. Put on headphones for a clean one.
recorderPage.stepsTitle: How to record in the app
steps: Create an account on the site, sign in, download the installer, open the shortcut and sign in to the app with the same address.
Pick a beat. Put on headphones. Press the mic test and check that the level is good when you speak.
Set the count-in, press Record, then Stop. The file stays on this computer, in the app data.
Cut and move the recordings on the timeline. Set volume and pan. Play uses the chosen output.
Press Done and send the recording to Studio. Finish the song on the site: clips, effects, mix and master.
recorderPage.siteLead: In the browser you record in two places: on a published beat page, or inside a Studio project. You also finish the song there.
siteDoes: On the beat page you make a quick take on a published beat, inside the plan time limit.
In Studio you open a project, record more tracks and place them on the timeline.
You cut clips and set volume, pan, automation and notes.
You hear the effects in the mix on the site. From Silver you also get pitch other than zero, ducking under the beat, and splitting a beat into stems.
You ask BITEK for a mix and a master. BITEK does that itself. The master preview carries the Bit Rym Dym watermark. You approve the master.
You ask Bitek in Studio for the mix, then the master. There is no separate mailbox to a person.
Export, a private listen link, a cover and video stay on the site.
You upload your own beat on the site. The app does not publish it.
recorderPage.limitsLead: The app and the site read the same plan. The beat does not use a recording-track slot.
recorderPage.limitsNote: Ducking under the beat: when the beat hits, the vocal dips for a moment so you still hear the beat. Pitch means raising or lowering the whole take. Both start on Silver. Stems do too. Free and Bronze have a shorter take and fewer tracks. Prices and the rest of the plan are on the Premium page.

intro.boom-bap: Boom bap is rap's classic sound: a heavy kick, a dry, punchy snare, vinyl samples and a swinging bounce. Tempo usually sits around 85–95 BPM, leaving room for dense bars and storytelling.
intro.hip-hop: Hip-hop covers a lot of ground, from classic drums to cleaner modern production. These beats work for verses, hooks and freestyles, and the mid tempo lets you rap laid-back or push double time.
intro.lo-fi-hip-hop: Lo-fi hip-hop is warm and dusty: tape hiss, muffled keys, soft drums and a loose groove. The slower tempo and calm mood suit reflective lyrics, melodic flows and relaxed sessions.
intro.trap: Trap means heavy 808s, fast hi-hat rolls and dark melodies. Tempo is usually written as 130–160 BPM, but the drums play half-time, so your flow can be lazy or fast with triplets.

loudness.title: Loudness
loudness.ok: Overall {lufs} LUFS, 3 s max {st} LUFS. Mastering sets the rest.
loudness.silent: No sound at all. Check that the tracks aren't muted.
loudness.quiet: The mix is very quiet ({lufs} LUFS). Turn the tracks up.
loudness.hot: The mix is already very loud ({lufs} LUFS). Leave room for mastering.

balance.title: Vocal vs beat
balance.ok: The vocal is {lu} LU against the beat. That's right.
balance.noBeat: There's no beat in the project, so nothing to compare the vocal with.
balance.noVocal: There's no vocal in the project. Record one or set a track role.
balance.vocalBuried: The vocal gets lost in the beat ({lu} LU). Turn the vocal up or the beat down.
balance.vocalTooLoud: The vocal is much louder than the beat ({lu} LU). The beat sounds like background.
balance.vocalLow: The vocal is a bit too quiet against the beat ({lu} LU).
balance.vocalHigh: The vocal is a bit too loud against the beat ({lu} LU).

presence.title: Word clarity
presence.na: No vocal or beat to compare.
presence.ok: The words are clear. In the speech range the vocal leads by {db} dB.
presence.weak: The words are hard to make out. The vocal leads the speech range by only {db} dB.
presence.covered: The beat covers the words (speech range {db} dB). The vocal needs room.

masking.title: Masking
masking.na: No vocal or beat to compare.
masking.ok: The beat rarely covers the vocal ({pct}% of the time).
masking.some: The beat sometimes covers the vocal ({pct}% of the time).
masking.heavy: The vocal blends into the beat {pct}% of the time.

sibilance.title: Sibilance (s, sh)
sibilance.ok: The s and sh sounds are natural.
sibilance.some: The s and sh sounds are a bit sharp ({db} dB).
sibilance.harsh: The s and sh sounds hurt the ears ({db} dB).

clipping.title: Clipping
clipping.clipped: The recording clips ({events} spots). Turn the track down or record quieter.
clipping.overPeak: The mix goes over 0 dB ({tp} dBTP). Turn the tracks or the master down.
clipping.fewClips: A few short clips ({events}). Turn the loudest track down a little.
clipping.lowHeadroom: Little headroom for mastering (peak {tp} dBTP). Turn the mix down 2–3 dB.

noise.title: Background noise
noise.na: Not enough recorded vocal to judge noise.

stereo.title: Stereo
stereo.ok: Stereo is healthy (correlation {corr}). It will sound fine on a phone too.
stereo.wide: The mix is very wide (correlation {corr}). Something may vanish on a single speaker.
stereo.phase: The channels cancel out (correlation {corr}). Part of the sound will vanish on a phone.

panorama.title: Ad-libs and doubles
panorama.ok: Ad-libs and doubles are spread to the sides and the lead vocal is centred.
panorama.noAdlibs: No ad-libs or doubles. The lead vocal is centred.
panorama.leadOffCentre: The lead vocal isn't centred ({names}). Move it to the middle.
panorama.adlibsCentred: Ad-libs sit in the middle ({names}). Spread them to the sides.
panorama.oneSide: All ad-libs are on one side. Spread them left and right.

mixStep.harmoniaOpis: A quiet note under the main vocal and another above it. The main vocal stays in front.
mixStep.wyrownanieOpis: Quiet words come up toward the loud ones. The pause stays quiet.
mixStep.poglosOpis: A short tempo echo and a light reverb. The words stay in front.
mixStep.glosOpis: The same voice: lower, higher, or a phone band. The color slider is on the track.
mixStep.novaOpis: Bitek turns the measurement, the pocket and the vocal level. Harmony stays its own button.

mixStep.nutkiGotowe: Added {count, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}} to “{track}”. Undo with Ctrl+Z.
mixStep.bladSciezka: Could not load the recording on “{track}”. Check the connection and try again, or mute that track.

notes.chainFull: “{track}” already has a full set of effects, so I didn't add anything there.
notes.planLimit: Your plan fits {max, plural, one {# effect} other {# effects}} on “{track}”, so I skipped some of the fixes.
notes.duck: I set the beat so its middle steps back a little while you rap. The voice stays as it is.
notes.pocket: I warmed the vocal and made room for the rap: the verse sits back, the hook comes closer, the middle of the beat steps back, and a quiet second voice is on the hook.
notes.rider: I leveled the vocal: quiet words up, loud words down, and the pause stays quiet.
notes.harmony: I added a second, quieter note under the vocal and above it. The main voice stays in front.
notes.voice: I added a voice color on the lead. Same voice: lower, higher, or a phone band.
notes.tune: I added light pitch correction on the lead (natural style). Notes sit closer to the key, without a hard trap snap.
notes.gainClipTrack: I turned “{track}” down {db} dB because it was clipping. Now it has headroom.
notes.gainTrimTrack: I turned “{track}” down {db} dB so it doesn't hit zero.
notes.gainMasterDown: I turned the whole mix down {db} dB to leave headroom for mastering.
notes.gainMasterUp: I turned the whole mix up {db} dB because it was too quiet to work with.
notes.balanceVocalUp: I turned your vocal up {up} dB and the beat down {down} dB so your vocal sits on top.
notes.balanceVocalDown: I turned the vocal down {down} dB and gave the beat {up} dB so the beat doesn't sound like background.
notes.balanceVocalOnlyUp: I turned your vocal up {up} dB and left the beat as loud as it was.
notes.balanceBeatOnlyDown: I turned the beat down {down} dB because the vocal would clip any louder.
notes.balanceVocalOnlyDown: I turned the vocal down {down} dB because the beat has no room to go up.
notes.balanceVocalDrawn: I left the fader of “{track}” alone, because it has a drawn volume curve. It needs about {db} dB more: raise the curve or clear it.
notes.balanceVocalTooQuiet: Your vocal was recorded very quietly: it is still {db} dB short. I won't turn the beat down any further, so try recording louder.
notes.balanceSideDown: I turned “{track}” down {db} dB. It should sit about {under} dB under the lead so it doesn't cover the words.
notes.balanceSideUp: I turned “{track}” up {db} dB. You should hear it, about {under} dB under the lead.
notes.compLead: I added a compressor on “{track}” ({ratio}:1). Your vocal stays even and the words don't get lost.
notes.compSide: I added a gentle compressor on “{track}” ({ratio}:1) so it sits evenly in the back.
notes.eqBeatCut: I turned the beat “{track}” down {db} dB in the mids (around 2.5 kHz) so your vocal sits better.
notes.eqVocalHighpass: I cut the rumble below {hz} Hz on “{track}”. The vocal sounds cleaner and the bass has room.
notes.eqVocalPresence: On “{track}” I took out some boom (250 Hz) and added 2 dB of clarity (3.5 kHz).
notes.deesserSoft: I softened the harsh s and sh on “{track}”.
notes.deesserStrong: I softened the harsh s and sh on “{track}” more. They don't sting now.
notes.denoiseGate: I added a gentle gate on “{track}”. Noise in the pauses is quieter (up to {db} dB).
notes.denoiseRumble: I also cut low noise below {hz} Hz on “{track}”.
notes.panLeadCenter: I put “{track}” in the centre. The lead vocal belongs in the middle.
notes.panLeft: I moved “{track}” left ({pct}%) to make room for the lead vocal.
notes.panRight: I moved “{track}” right ({pct}%) to make room for the lead vocal.
notes.spaceLead: I added a short echo ({note} note, {ms} ms at {bpm} BPM) and a light reverb on “{track}”. The vocal isn't dry and the words stay up front.
notes.spaceSide: I added reverb ({decay} s) and an echo in time with the beat ({note} note, {ms} ms) on “{track}”. Your adlibs make space behind you.

msg.recording: Recording. Focus on the performance — I won't touch the faders here.
msg.chooseBeat: Hi! Start by choosing the beat you'll record on.

msg.keysIdle: Turn on record and click a key. I'll say whether the line stays close.
msg.keysShort: You have {count, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}}. Add a few more so I can hear a phrase.
msg.keysSame: You're holding one note. Click a neighbour and the line will move.
msg.keysLeap: That's a big jump. Closer keys sit together more easily.
msg.keysDrumsOne: I hear one drum piece. Add a kick and a snare.
msg.keysDrumsOk: Kick and snare are in. This already holds the tempo.
msg.keysLineOk: The line stays close and it moves. It can go on like this.
msg.keysScratch: The scratch is on this track. On play it sits in the beat with the rest.

msg.takeClip: The take is hitting the ceiling (peak {db} dB). I'll turn the track down in the mix. The clipped audio itself has to be recorded again.
msg.handoffQuiet: From the take: the vocal was quiet (peak {db} dB). I'll raise that track from the measurement. Nothing changes until you click.
msg.handoffClip: From the take: the signal clipped (peak {db} dB). I'll turn the track down so it stops slamming. Click if you want me to.
msg.handoffMissing: I don't see a vocal recording, so there's nothing to turn up. Record a vocal and come back.
msg.mixNeedsVocal: I need at least one recording to mix. Go back to recording.

msg.mixFailed: I couldn't analyze the mix. Let's try again.
msg.mixStale: Something changed since the last analysis. I'll check again.
msg.mixHasRed: {count, plural, one {One thing needs} other {# things need}} fixing before mastering. Let's start with the most important.
msg.mixHasYellow: No red items. {count, plural, one {One thing is} other {# things are}} still worth polishing.
msg.mixAllGreen: All good! The vocal sits well on the beat.
msg.mixReadyForMaster: You can go on to mastering.

fix.clipping: Clipping: pull the clipping track's volume down 3–6 dB. If the recording itself clips, record that part quieter.
fix.balance: Vocal vs beat: move the vocal or beat volume until the vocal is 0–3 LU above the beat.
fix.presence: Clarity: turn the vocal up or the beat down 2–3 dB. In the vocal EQ, lift around 3 kHz a little.
fix.masking: Masking: turn the beat down 2 dB or cut its mids (1–4 kHz) in the beat EQ.
fix.noise: Noise: record somewhere quieter, closer to the mic. The Mix step has noise quieting and vocal cleanup.
fix.sibilance: Sibilance: angle the mic slightly away from your mouth or lower the highs (6–8 kHz) in the vocal EQ.
fix.stereo: Stereo: check no track is phase-inverted and narrow the widest tracks.
fix.panorama: Panorama: keep the lead vocal centred, pan ad-libs left and right by 30–60.
fix.loudness: Loudness: set the faders so the mix is neither too quiet nor clipping.

msg.songLimit: A song can be at most {max} — I can't record past that. Trim it or move on to the mix.
msg.latencyBluetooth: You're on Bluetooth headphones — the vocal may lag. I'll calibrate it in 7 seconds.
msg.latencyHigh: I see {ms} ms of latency. Let's calibrate so the vocal sits on the beat.
msg.latencyDetail: Clicks through a speaker or clapping along. You can also set it by hand.
msg.liveHot: You're recording too loud. Back off the mic a little and keep the same level.
msg.liveQuiet: Too quiet. Move closer to the mic and commit to the vocal.
msg.liveUneven: The level is jumping. Record more evenly — stay the same distance from the mic.
msg.liveOffbeat: You're missing the beat. Listen for the kick and come in on the one.
msg.autoNeedBoth: Auto mix needs a beat and a recorded vocal. Choose a beat first, then record the vocal.
msg.autoNeedVocal: The beat is in. Record a raw vocal — once it's there, one click mixes the whole song.
msg.autoNeedBeat: The vocal is in. Choose a beat and I can mix the song.
msg.autoReady: Vocal and beat are ready. Click and I'll mix the whole song — everything the measurement can fix.
msg.autoMixTrwa: Mixing. I'm fixing everything the measurement can fix.
msg.autoMixGotowy: Mix is ready. Have a listen. Master it?
msg.autoMixNiegotowy: I did what I could automatically, but the mix is not ready for mastering yet: red items left: {count}. Use the Fix buttons on the cards below. Then we move on to mastering.

akcja.down: turns the track down by {db} dB
akcja.up: turns the track up by {db} dB

uwagi.ok: Loudness and peak are fine for every service. Nothing to fix.
uwagi.tpOver: Peak {tp} dBTP is over the safe {ceiling} dBTP. It can crackle after MP3/AAC encoding. Lower the master loudness by 1 step.
uwagi.loud: It is loud ({lufs} LUFS). Services will turn it down by about {down} dB, so the loudness gains nothing and you lose dynamics. Lower the loudness by 1–2 steps.
uwagi.quiet: It is quiet ({lufs} LUFS). Some services will not turn it up, so it will sound weaker than other tracks. Raise the loudness by 1–2 steps.
uwagi.squashed: Dynamics are heavily squashed (PLR {plr}). Reduce the squash or the loudness so the track is not flat.
uwagi.phase: Stereo correlation {corr}: on a phone or in mono part of the sound may vanish. Reduce the width.
